text:
dana: Quick sync on 'stitch' private-upgrade flow. Goals: predictable upgrades, preserve peering IPs, support offline bundles.

riya: Customer wants single-command dry-run and machine-readable plan. Example: `redwoodctl plan-upgrade --bundle stitch.tar.gz --dry-run --out plan.json`.

oscar: For airgapped sites: signed offline bundle + small manifest. Keep manifest minimal (version, components, deltas).

dana: Proposed GA checklist: 1) signed offline bundle + sha checks, 2) net-claim metadata (optional) with owner and preserve_ips flag, 3) `redwoodctl plan-upgrade --dry-run` with conflicts output, 4) canary -> ramp -> full rollout and rollback snapshot, 5) ops runbook + field checklist.

riya: Net-claim example shape for docs: `{\"subnet\":\"10.0.3.0/24\",\"owner\":\"netops@cust.co\",\"preserve_ips\":true}` stored as string so older agents skip. Include TTL for claims.

oscar: QA: add peering-preserve test to nightly matrix, simulate external peer and validate nodePort/IP mapping after upgrade.

dana: Action items: @riya spec net-claim + docs, @oscar prototype offline bundle + manifest, @dana assemble runbook and schedule customer review. Patch-bot: created doc link https://docs.redwood.ai/stitch.

oscar: +1 to opt-in `--simulate-peer-loss` in dry-run to surface BGP risks (default off).

dana: Thanks, will send calendar invite for customer review. :white_check_mark:
